title: CottonBot: An AI-driven cotton farming assistant and irrigation advisor using LLM-RAG and agentic AI tools
relevance_reason: Vector databases (FAISS and Chroma) are used only as retrieval backends within the RAG pipeline of an agricultural AI assistant; the brief comparison between them serves the application rather than studying vector database technology itself.
research_focus: Design and evaluation of CottonBot, an AI-driven cotton farming assistant that integrates RAG with agentic LLM tools and real-time sensor data to provide agronomic guidance and irrigation recommendations to cotton farmers.
method: A hybrid architecture combining a RAG pipeline (with FAISS and Chroma as retrieval backends, multiple embedding models, and Llama 3.1 via Ollama for generation) with agentic tool calling for real-time soil moisture and weather data integration, deployed as a cross-platform mobile app using FastAPI and Flutter.
mentioned_systems: FAISS; Chroma; Ollama; Llama 3.1; Llama2; Phi3; Gemma3; FastAPI; Flutter; all-MiniLM-L6-v2; bge-m3; e5-mistral-7binstruct; AgroLLM; BeefBot
application_domain: Precision agriculture / cotton farming (pest management, soil fertilization, weed control, irrigation recommendations)
results_summary: The paper evaluated CottonBot's RAG pipeline by comparing FAISS and Chroma as retrieval backends across multiple embedding models, finding that FAISS consistently outperformed Chroma in MRR, Recall@5, and Precision@5, with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 achieving the best retrieval performance. In the generation phase, Llama 3.1 produced the most faithful and semantically accurate responses, while smaller models like Phi3 and Gemma3 were faster but less accurate. The agentic tools for real-time irrigation recommendations, using soil moisture sensors and weather APIs with cotton-specific thresholds (45 kPa soil tension), demonstrated utility beyond static text retrieval. The system was deployed as a cross-platform mobile application, and results indicated improved decision-making support, more efficient water use, and improved crop yields for cotton farmers.
limitations: LLM-based systems can still produce hallucinated or partially inaccurate statements when queries fall outside the retrieved context; Smaller models like Phi3 and Gemma3 exhibited a noticeable drop in factual alignment and semantic coherence compared to Llama 3.1; The system is currently limited to cotton-specific knowledge and does not yet support other crops or livestock
research_gaps: Expand CottonBot to support additional crops (peanuts, corn) and livestock as a general Agri-Bot; Incorporate a voice recognition engine for verbal queries; Introduce an automated feedback feature; Improve the irrigation decision model by training the soil moisture prediction model with larger and more diverse datasets; Perform on-field trials to monitor onsite performance for the 2026 farming season

title: AUTOMATED BLOOM’S TAXONOMY-BASED QUESTION GENERATION FOR COURSE OUTCOME ATTAINMENT IN OBE FRAMEWORKS
relevance_reason: The vector database is used solely as a retrieval component within a RAG pipeline for educational question generation; the paper does not propose, analyze, benchmark, or discuss vector database technology, indexing methods, or system comparisons in any depth.
research_focus: Automated generation of Bloom's Taxonomy-based assessment questions aligned with Course Outcomes in Outcome-Based Education (OBE) frameworks, using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system grounded in private educational materials.
method: A RAG pipeline that stores scanned textbooks, syllabi, and CO annotations as SBERT embeddings in a vector database for retrieval, then uses an LLM to generate questions constrained to the syllabus scope. A validation module classifies generated questions by Bloom's level and checks CO alignment via semantic similarity. The system was implemented in Python and demonstrated on a Blockchain Technology course.
application_domain: Educational assessment and question generation in Outcome-Based Education
results_summary: The system was demonstrated on a Blockchain Technology course, generating questions at specified Bloom's Taxonomy levels (e.g., Analysis) aligned with specific Course Outcomes. Expert panel evaluation showed 97% syllabus relevance, 93% Bloom's Taxonomy alignment, and 95% CO attainment. The automated process was reported to significantly reduce manual effort and ensure comprehensive coverage of all COs and cognitive levels. The authors conclude the approach overcomes limitations of generic LLMs by grounding generation in private, syllabus-specific content.
research_gaps: Scaling the system across multiple subjects and educational institutions

title: Sustainable Bites Leveraging AI to Decode Food Emissions and Nutrition for Conscious Consumption
relevance_reason: The vector database is used only as a storage and retrieval component at the end of an AI/food-sustainability pipeline; the paper does not propose, analyze, benchmark, or discuss vector database technology, indexing methods, or system comparisons in any depth.
research_focus: An AI-driven framework that uses open-source LLMs to approximate ingredient compositions of processed food products, combines these with emissions databases and NutriScore to create a dataset of GHG impact and nutritional value, and stores the results in a vector database for real-time consumer recommendations of healthier, lower-impact alternatives.
method: LLaMA3 is used to infer recipes from product descriptions and ingredient lists; the USDA Global Branded Food Products Database provides base data; GHG emissions are estimated from public databases and model-generated approximations; NutriScore is applied for nutritional assessment; sentence-transformer models generate embeddings; all data is stored in a vector database for similarity search and filtering.
mentioned_systems: LLaMA3; USDA Global Branded Food Products Database; NutriScore
application_domain: Food sustainability and consumer dietary recommendations (greenhouse gas emissions and nutritional assessment of processed food products)
results_summary: The authors built a pipeline that uses LLaMA3 to estimate ingredient compositions of over 400,000 food products from the USDA database, then computed GHG emission scores and NutriScores for each product. Because no comprehensive joint dataset of emissions and nutrition existed, a quantitative benchmark was not feasible, so evaluation was done through qualitative validation against domain knowledge (e.g., confirming pepperoni pizza scores higher in emissions than vegetarian alternatives). The computed data, including semantic embeddings, is stored in a vector database to enable real-time similarity queries and recommendations. The framework demonstrates that LLMs can bridge the knowledge gap of proprietary recipe data and that the resulting vector database supports practical consumer-facing retrieval of lower-impact, healthier alternatives.
limitations: Emission assessment is constrained to greenhouse gas outputs and does not incorporate water usage, land exploitation, or biodiversity effects; The framework operates independently of economic considerations such as price, which is a major factor in consumer behavior; A quantitative benchmark was not feasible due to the lack of a comprehensive dataset jointly including GHG emissions and nutritional metrics for processed foods
research_gaps: Incorporate broader environmental indicators (water usage, land exploitation, biodiversity) into the emission assessment; Integrate supply chain transparency mechanisms such as blockchain; Explore region-specific optimizations for diverse food markets and geographies; Incorporate cost-based filtering into the vector database alongside nutritional and emission metrics; Align the platform with emerging global standards in sustainable consumption and digital food labeling
